entities.summary: The Medium Diesel Engine (MDE) is a four-cylinder diesel engine developed by General Motors and branded "1.6 CDTI Ecotec" in most markets. Opel also adds the marketing term "Whisper Diesel" in some markets, claiming relatively low levels of noise, vibration, and harshness. Production commenced in late 2013 at Szentgotthárd, Hungary. The MDE is Opel's first all-aluminum diesel engine and offers a power density of 85 hp (63 kW) per liter 136 PS in its most powerful version. Maximum power and torque have been increased versus the previous-generation 1.7-liter engine, while fuel consumption has been reduced by up to 10 percent compared with a 2.0-liter CDTI engine of similar power output.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Medium Diesel Engine's increased power density and reduced fuel consumption had a regional impact on the automotive industry, contributing to Opel's competitiveness in the European market. Its adoption by various car manufacturers also influenced the development of more efficient diesel engines.
